ledger.note: 343: Artaxerxes III reconquers Egypt and the Thirty-first Dynasty begins. His campaign began about 351 and the first attempt failed ("Nectanebo inflicted a crushing defeat on the Persians"); Nectanebo II was "out-manoeuvered and defeated by the combined Persian armies near Pelusium", "hastily fled to Memphis" and then fled south, after which all Egypt submitted. The page dates the satrapy "between 343 BC to 332 BC".
338: Khababash revolts in Upper Egypt and declares himself pharaoh; the table says he "Led a revolt against Persian rule in Upper Egypt, declared himself Pharaoh" (338–335).
335: Upper Egypt is recovered: the table says "Upper Egypt returned to Persian control in 335 BC".

region.text: Egypt, the whole Nile Valley and Delta

ledger.note: 332: Mazaces gives Egypt to Alexander. The page: "In 332 BC, Mazaces handed over the country to Alexander the Great without a fight."
332: the Thirty-first Dynasty ends; Alexander the Great holds Egypt, which the Ptolemies take as their kingdom from 331.

wars.name: Artaxerxes III's reconquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Persian victory in 343 after a failed attempt about 351; Nectanebo II was beaten near Pelusium and fled to Ethiopia (Nubia); Artaxerxes III razed the walls, looted the temples and appointed Pherendates satrap.
wars.note: The page dates the first attempt to about 351 BC; neither the Sidon revolt nor Bubastis is on the page. [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] from moved -351 to -343 to keep the war inside this dossier's life (343-332); the failed campaign of about 351 was against the Thirtieth Dynasty and belongs to its dossier.

wars.name: Revolt of Khababash
wars.outcome: Khababash held Upper Egypt as pharaoh for three years; it returned to Persian control in 335.
wars.note: The table gives 338–335; the page says nothing of the fighting.

wars.name: Alexander's conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: No fighting: Mazaces handed Egypt over in 332.

certainty.note: No frontier is given; only Egypt, Lower and Upper Egypt are named.

notes:
Second Persian period, 343-332. Egypt as a land (family egypt). fx-34 (F332): the first draft carried the Persian rule as an occupation pair naming achaemenid-empire (ledger /1 and /5 of that draft, 343 and 332), hatched over Egypt; both were removed because the Thirty-first Dynasty page calls the period 'effectively a satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire between 343 BC to 332 BC' and data/hierarchy.csv already draws this state as a constituent of achaemenid-empire (R3), and the achaemenid-empire dossier draws Egypt as its own land (ledger /35 gain 343, /39 loss 332), so the occupation hatch drew Egypt a second time. The event indexes after /0 moved down by one (the loss to Khababash is now /1, its recovery /2, the 332 loss /3, the dissolve /4). The hierarchy row is clamped to -338..-333; the dossiers hold the relation for -343..-332 (handoff to extend the row). me-03-c's Thirtieth Dynasty ends 343 with the loss to achaemenid-empire. The Second Achaemenid conquest page (not opened) reportedly gives 340/339; the 31st page and the Egypt (satrapy) page's 343-332 agree. The Egypt (satrapy) page also says the second period ran 'between 358 and 330 BC' in its body, inconsistent with its own 343-332.

Khababash (338-335) held land for three years and has his own rebel dossier (khababash). The Khababash page argues he held all or almost all of Egypt (a contract at Thebes, a decree naming Buto, an Apis sarcophagus at Saqqara); this dossier follows the 31st page's rulers table (Upper Egypt to Khababash, Lower Egypt to Artaxerxes IV). Mazaces is spelled as the page gives it.
